title: Open Hardware Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Hardware designs, bills of materials, licenses, assembly instructions, and test reports. The Open Hardware Database documents hardware anyone can build: complete designs (schematics, PCB layouts, mechanical files), bills of materials with sourcing, the open license covering the design, step-by-step assembly instructions, and test reports from actual builds. Open hardware lives or dies on reproducibility — each record includes everything needed to build one, and the test report from someone who did.

Test reports: build logs, measurements, issues found, fixes

title: Open Hardware Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Open hardware anatomy: DESIGN FILES (schematic, PCB Gerbers, mechanical CAD, firmware) versioned together; BOM (part, spec, qty, sources, alternates); LICENSE (CERN-OHL variants: strongly reciprocal; TAPR; Solderpad — what sharing modifications requires); ASSEMBLY (ordered steps, tools needed, skill level, test points); TEST REPORT (build log, measurements vs spec, issues + fixes). Documentation standard: someone skilled but unfamiliar must succeed — the test builds prove it. Sourcing: LCSC/DigiKey/Mouser-class options with part numbers; alternates for stock-outs. Safety: mains isolation, battery handling, ESD — flagged per design. Community: issue tracking per design; improvements as new versions.

title: Open Hardware Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: BOM test (all parts specified with sources); license test (terms stated); assembly test (steps ordered, tools listed); evidence test (test reports include measurements). Limitations: designs need physical builds to verify (test reports are the evidence); component markets shift; safety review per use. Every design carries version and last-build date.

demo.title: Verification: trade-off scoring and sensitivity
demo.code: const opts={A:{perf:9,rel:6,simple:5},B:{perf:6,rel:9,simple:8}};const w={perf:0.5,rel:0.3,simple:0.2};function score(o){return o.perf*w.perf+o.rel*w.rel+o.simple*w.simple;}const sA=score(opts.A),sB=score(opts.B);const w2={perf:0.3,rel:0.5,simple:0.2};function score2(o){return o.perf*w2.perf+o.rel*w2.rel+o.simple*w2.simple;}const flip=score2(opts.B)>score2(opts.A);J({sA:+sA.toFixed(2),sB:+sB.toFixed(2),flip});assert(sA>sB&&flip,'tradeoff');

Finally, run the demo program for this record and confirm the output matches the verified output before moving on.
